courses.name: Make it from wood
courses.why: Making a shelf, a box or a bench is a skill that saves money and builds confidence.

courses.name: Draw it before you make it
courses.why: A quick drawing prevents costly mistakes in any project or repair.

courses.name: Sew, mend and make clothes
courses.why: Mending and altering clothes saves money and extends life of what you own.
units: Fixing a hem and a button

courses.name: Books and journals by hand
courses.why: A hand-bound notebook or a repaired favorite book is a lasting gift.

courses.name: Design, build, test
courses.why: Every making project goes through the same loop; knowing it helps people stop guessing.

sources.title: Design and Manufacturing I (2.007, Spring 2009)
sources.by: Prof. Daniel Frey and Prof. David Gossard, MIT
sources.licenceSeen: OCW course page footer links the Creative Commons licence; OCW Terms page states CC BY-NC-SA 4.0
sources.terms: OCW Terms page: content may be used to train and improve AI models with attribution, non-commercial use only, and derived models must carry CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 or a compatible licence.
sources.needIt: Shows the whole path from an idea to a working thing: sketching, picking materials, building, testing and fixing.
sources.notes: Undergraduate; students build a robot. OCW lists competition videos but no lecture videos. Needs plain-level rebuild.

sources.title: How to Make (Almost) Anything (MAS.863, Fall 2002)
sources.by: Prof. Isaac Chuang and Prof. Neil Gershenfeld, MIT
sources.licenceSeen: OCW course page footer links the Creative Commons licence; OCW Terms page states CC BY-NC-SA 4.0
sources.terms: OCW Terms page: content may be used to train and improve AI models with attribution, non-commercial use only, and derived models must carry CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 or a compatible licence.
sources.needIt: Shows how digital tools like laser cutters, 3D printers and circuit boards let one person make nearly anything.
sources.notes: GRADUATE course; no videos on OCW. Fall 2002 tools are dated; the current MIT class is by permission and is not on OCW (search result only, not verified here).

sources.title: Wood-working for Beginners: A Manual for Amateurs
sources.licenceSeen: Project Gutenberg ebook page, Copyright line reads 'Public domain in the USA.'
sources.needIt: Starter projects with tools, measuring and joints, a base for any wood project.
sources.notes: Old safety practice (no guards, dust masks or eye protection). Add current notes.

sources.title: Carpentry for Boys
sources.licenceSeen: Project Gutenberg ebook page, Copyright line reads 'Public domain in the USA.'
sources.needIt: Beginner builds like a workbench, with steps in plain talk.
sources.notes: Title and tone are dated and gendered; rewrite for everyone. Old finishes may be lead based; modern safety needed.

sources.title: Things To Make
sources.licenceSeen: Project Gutenberg ebook page, Copyright line reads 'Public domain in the USA.'
sources.needIt: Dozens of small projects from toys to electrical gadgets.
sources.notes: Some projects use dangerous mains voltage or old chemicals; keep only low risk ones and flag the rest.

sources.title: Bookbinding, and the Care of Books
sources.licenceSeen: Project Gutenberg ebook page, Copyright line reads 'Public domain in the USA.'
sources.needIt: Teaches how a book is sewn and bound, which helps with repairing, journals and gifts.
sources.notes: Some tools (lying press, tools for gilding) are rare; list low cost substitutes.

sources.title: Bookbinding for Beginners
sources.by: Florence O. Bean and John C. Brodhead
sources.licenceSeen: Project Gutenberg ebook page, Copyright line reads 'Public domain in the USA.'
sources.needIt: A first project path: folded sheets, a simple cover, a small notebook.
sources.notes: First published 1918 per the Gutenberg page. Old glues and cutting tools need modern safety notes.

sources.title: The ladies' complete guide to crochet, fancy knitting, and needlework
sources.licenceSeen: Project Gutenberg ebook page, Copyright line reads 'Public domain in the USA.'
sources.needIt: Patterns and stitch instructions for knitting, crochet and mending that are still used.
sources.notes: First published 1854 per the Gutenberg page. Pattern language is old shorthand; modern patterns differ. Fibers and dyes of the day may be unsafe.

sources.title: Dress design: an account of costume for artists & dressmakers
sources.licenceSeen: Project Gutenberg ebook page, Copyright line reads 'Public domain in the USA.'
sources.needIt: Explains how clothing is shaped and drawn, helpful for altering and making clothes.
sources.notes: Costume history is Western and dated. Focus on pattern and fit.

sources.title: The home dressmakers' guide
sources.licenceSeen: Archive page: 'The Library of Congress is unaware of any copyright restrictions for this item.'
sources.needIt: Teaches measuring, cutting and sewing a garment at home, a skill that saves money.
sources.notes: Patterns are 1919 fashions; teach the method, not the styles.

sources.title: Mechanical drawing for industrial and high schools
sources.licenceSeen: Archive page: 'The Library of Congress is unaware of any copyright restrictions for this item.'
sources.needIt: Teaches how to draw an object so someone else can build it, the first step of any make.
sources.notes: Pencil, T-square and ink drawing; modern drawing is on a screen. Keep the lines, views and dimension rules.

sources.title: Shop sketching, a course of problems for mechanical drawing students
sources.licenceSeen: Archive metadata field 'possible-copyright-status: NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT' (the item's details page was not opened).
sources.needIt: Quick freehand sketches for planning a part or a repair.
sources.notes: Details page not opened; confirm the status on the page before building.
